note: Svasthaiḥ can mean healthy, composed or secure; the translation keeps a broad ‘at ease’ sense and treats promised effects as the hymn’s devotional claim.

english: ‘With these enemies slain, the world attains happiness. Though they have committed sin that could keep them in hell for long, perhaps by meeting death in battle they may reach heaven—surely it is with this thought that you destroy your foes, O Goddess.’
hindi: ‘इन शत्रुओं के मारे जाने से जगत् सुख पाता है। यद्यपि उन्होंने ऐसे पाप किए हैं जो उन्हें दीर्घकाल नरक में ले जाएँ, फिर भी युद्ध में मृत्यु पाकर वे स्वर्ग जा सकें—हे देवी, निश्चय ही ऐसा सोचकर आप शत्रुओं का वध करती हैं।’
note: The verse’s syntax and transmitted readings are debated; this source-attributed theology of battle death is not a Devam ethical endorsement or guidance for real-world violence.

english: ‘Why do you not reduce all the asuras to ashes merely by looking at them? Because you send weapons against your foes so that even they, purified by weapons, may reach higher worlds—such is your exceedingly benevolent intention even toward them.’
hindi: ‘आप केवल दृष्टि से ही सभी असुरों को भस्म क्यों नहीं कर देतीं? आप शत्रुओं पर शस्त्र इसलिए चलाती हैं कि वे भी शस्त्रों से पवित्र होकर उच्च लोकों को प्राप्त करें—उनके प्रति भी आपकी ऐसी परम साधु भावना है।’
note: This is the hymn’s theological explanation of the Goddess’s weapons, not a general doctrine that violent death purifies people.

english: ‘That the asuras’ eyes were not destroyed by the fierce flashes of your sword’s radiance or the massed brilliance of your spear-point was because they were beholding your face, fit to be compared with a fragment of the radiant moon.’
hindi: ‘आपके खड्ग की तीव्र चमक और शूलाग्र की प्रखर कान्ति से असुरों की आँखें नष्ट नहीं हुईं, क्योंकि वे आपके उस मुख को देख रहे थे जो दीप्तिमान चन्द्रकला के समान था।’
note: The Sanskrit is syntactically compressed; this follows the comparison witness’s causal reading while preserving the moon-fragment simile.

english: ‘Your nature, O Goddess, restrains the conduct of the ill-behaved; this form of yours is inconceivable and unequalled by others. Your valour destroys those who stole the gods’ power, yet in this way you have visibly shown compassion even toward enemies.’
hindi: ‘हे देवी, आपका स्वभाव दुराचारियों के आचरण का शमन करता है; आपका यह रूप अचिन्त्य और अनुपम है। आपका पराक्रम देवताओं का बल छीनने वालों का वध करता है, फिर भी आपने शत्रुओं पर भी इस प्रकार प्रत्यक्ष दया दिखाई है।’
note: The verse’s moral characterization remains the praising gods’ interpretation of the battle.

english: ‘What can compare with this valour of yours? Where else is there a form so captivating yet so fearsome to enemies? Compassion in your heart and severity in battle are seen together in you alone, O boon-giving Goddess, throughout the three worlds.’
hindi: ‘आपके इस पराक्रम की उपमा किससे हो? शत्रुओं को भय देने वाला होते हुए भी इतना मनोहर रूप और कहाँ है? हे वरदायिनी देवी, हृदय में करुणा और युद्ध में कठोरता तीनों लोकों में केवल आपमें साथ दिखाई देती हैं।’
note: The verse explicitly holds compassion and battle severity in tension; it is preserved as hymn theology, not simplified into a universal moral pattern.

english: ‘By destroying the foes at the head of battle you have protected all three worlds; by killing them you have also led the enemy hosts to heaven, and dispelled the fear caused in us by the frenzied enemies of the gods. We bow to you.’
hindi: ‘रणाग्र में शत्रुओं का नाश कर आपने सम्पूर्ण त्रैलोक्य की रक्षा की; उन्हें मारकर शत्रुगणों को स्वर्ग भी पहुँचाया और उन्मत्त देवशत्रुओं से उत्पन्न हमारा भय दूर किया। आपको नमस्कार है।’
note: The claimed heavenly destination continues the hymn’s battle theology and is not independently asserted by Devam.

english: ‘Protect us with your trident, O Goddess; protect us with your sword, O Ambikā. Protect us with the sound of your bell and with the twang of your bowstring.’
hindi: ‘हे देवी, त्रिशूल से हमारी रक्षा करें; हे अम्बिके, खड्ग से हमारी रक्षा करें। घंटा-नाद और धनुष की प्रत्यञ्चा के स्वर से हमारी रक्षा करें।’
note: This is a translated prayer within the hymn; it does not by itself define a complete ritual procedure.

english: ‘Guard us in the east and in the west; guard us in the south, O Caṇḍikā, and likewise in the north, O sovereign Goddess, by the circling of your trident.’
hindi: ‘पूर्व और पश्चिम में हमारी रक्षा करें; हे चण्डिके, दक्षिण में और हे ईश्वरि, अपने त्रिशूल को घुमाकर उत्तर में भी हमारी रक्षा करें।’
note: The directional plea is preserved as source prayer, not promoted into stand-alone protective instruction.

english: ‘By all your gentle forms that move through the three worlds, and by those that are exceedingly terrible, protect us and protect the earth.’
hindi: ‘तीनों लोकों में विचरण करने वाले आपके सभी सौम्य रूपों और अत्यन्त घोर रूपों से हमारी तथा पृथ्वी की रक्षा करें।’
note: The source embraces multiple gentle and fierce manifestations without requiring them to be collapsed into one iconography.

english: ‘With your sword, trident, mace and all the other weapons joined to your tender, leaf-like hands, O Ambikā, protect us on every side.’
hindi: ‘हे अम्बिके, आपके कोमल करपल्लवों में धारण खड्ग, त्रिशूल, गदा और अन्य सभी अस्त्र-शस्त्रों से चारों ओर हमारी रक्षा करें।’
note: The juxtaposition of tender hands and weapons is preserved as the source’s devotional imagery.

english: The sage said: ‘Praised in this way by the gods, the sustainer of the worlds was worshipped with celestial flowers grown in Nandana and with fragrant ointments.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘देवताओं द्वारा इस प्रकार स्तुति किए जाने पर जगत् की धात्री की नन्दनवन में उत्पन्न दिव्य पुष्पों और सुगन्धित अनुलेपों से पूजा की गई।’
note: The pinned narrator form ṛṣīr uvāca is orthographically irregular; context supports ṛṣir uvāca.

english: All the gods devoutly offered her celestial incense. With a gracious and serene face, she spoke to all the gods who bowed before her.
hindi: सभी देवताओं ने भक्तिपूर्वक उन्हें दिव्य धूप अर्पित की। प्रसन्न और कृपामय मुख वाली देवी ने अपने सामने झुके सभी देवताओं से कहा।
note: The pinned compound around tridasha and divya has a minor joining irregularity; the offering sequence remains clear.

english: The Goddess said: ‘All you gods, choose whatever you desire from me. Greatly pleased and well honoured by these hymns, I shall grant it.’
hindi: देवी ने कहा: ‘हे सभी देवताओं, मुझसे जो चाहो वह वर माँगो। इन स्तुतियों से सुन्दर रूप में पूजित और अत्यन्त प्रसन्न होकर मैं उसे दूँगी।’
note: The boon invitation is direct speech within the episode.

english: ‘We know of no other difficult task that remains to be done.’ Hearing these words of the Goddess, the dwellers in heaven replied.
hindi: ‘अब कोई अन्य कठिन कार्य करना शेष है, ऐसा हम नहीं जानते।’ देवी के ये वचन सुनकर स्वर्गवासियों ने उत्तर दिया।
note: Pargiter records this transition as edition-dependent; its speaker boundary is compressed in the pinned source, so the first sentence is kept distinct from the following gods’ formal reply.

english: The gods said: ‘The blessed Goddess has accomplished everything; nothing remains, for this Mahiṣāsura, our enemy, has been slain.’
hindi: देवताओं ने कहा: ‘भगवती ने सब कुछ कर दिया है; कुछ भी शेष नहीं रहा, क्योंकि हमारा शत्रु महिषासुर मारा गया है।’
note: The verse closes the gods’ immediate battle objective, not the broader Devī Māhātmya narrative.

english: ‘Yet if you would grant us a boon, O great sovereign Goddess, then whenever we remember you, please destroy our most terrible calamities.’
hindi: ‘फिर भी यदि आप हमें वर देना चाहती हैं, हे महेश्वरि, तो जब-जब हम आपका स्मरण करें, हमारी परम आपदाओं का नाश करें।’
note: The requested result is presented as the gods’ devotional boon, not a product guarantee for every recitation.

english: ‘And, O spotless-faced Ambikā, may you always be gracious to any mortal who praises you with these hymns, increasing that person’s prosperity in resources and abundance, including wealth, household and other forms of well-being.’
hindi: ‘हे निर्मलमुखी अम्बिके, जो मनुष्य इन स्तुतियों से आपकी स्तुति करे, उस पर सदा प्रसन्न होकर उसके धन, गृहस्थ-जीवन और अन्य सम्पदाओं की वृद्धि करें।’
note: The source lists wealth, spouse and other prosperity within its historical household frame; the translation broadens dāra to household life and treats the boon as source theology, not guaranteed financial advice.

english: The sage said: ‘Thus propitiated by the gods for the sake of the world and for themselves, Bhadrakālī said, “So be it,” and vanished, O king.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘जगत् और अपने हित के लिए देवताओं द्वारा इस प्रकार प्रसन्न की गई भद्रकाली ने “ऐसा ही हो” कहा और हे राजन्, अन्तर्धान हो गईं।’
note: The pinned jagator’rthe contains an orthographic joining irregularity; the parallel meaning ‘for the world and themselves’ is clear.

english: ‘Thus, O king, I have told you how in former times that Goddess, desiring the welfare of the three worlds, arose from the bodies of the gods.’
hindi: ‘इस प्रकार हे राजन्, मैंने बताया कि पूर्वकाल में तीनों लोकों का हित चाहने वाली वह देवी देवताओं के शरीरों से किस प्रकार प्रकट हुईं।’
note: This is the sage’s explicit retrospective boundary for the Mahiṣāsura episode.

english: ‘Hear now how she arose again from Gaurī’s body in order to slay the wicked daityas Śumbha and Niśumbha.’
hindi: ‘अब सुनो कि दुष्ट दैत्यों शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के वध के लिए वे गौरी के शरीर से पुनः किस प्रकार प्रकट हुईं।’
note: The source names the next manifestation’s bodily origin and adversaries, defining the transition to the following episode.

english: ‘As benefactress of the gods she arose also to protect the worlds. Listen: I shall relate it to you exactly as it occurred.’ Thus ends the eighty-fourth chapter in the Devī Māhātmya within the Sāvarṇika Manvantara of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Mahāpurāṇa.
hindi: ‘देवताओं का उपकार करने वाली वे लोकों की रक्षा के लिए भी प्रकट हुईं। सुनो, मैं तुम्हें वह वृत्तान्त यथावत् कहता हूँ।’ इस प्रकार श्रीमार्कण्डेयमहापुराण के सावर्णिक मन्वन्तर में देवीमाहात्म्य का चौरासीवाँ अध्याय समाप्त हुआ।
note: The pinned colophon has minor orthographic irregularities and no chapter title. Provider navigation residue ‘85(82)’ remains in the immutable span but is not translated as sacred text.

english: The sage said: ‘Long ago the asuras Śumbha and Niśumbha, relying on the pride of their strength, took the three worlds and the shares of sacrifice from the lord of Śacī.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘पूर्वकाल में असुर शुम्भ और निशुम्भ ने अपने बल के मद में शचीपति से तीनों लोक और यज्ञभाग छीन लिए।’
note: Lord of Śacī identifies Indra; the seizure is source narrative, not legitimate authority.

english: ‘The two of them likewise took over the Sun’s station and the Moon’s authority, as well as the offices of Kubera, Yama and Varuṇa.’
hindi: ‘उन दोनों ने सूर्य का पद, चन्द्रमा का अधिकार तथा कुबेर, यम और वरुण के पद भी अपने हाथ में ले लिए।’
note: The verse describes usurpation of cosmic offices, not a change in the asuras’ personal identities.

english: ‘They exercised the Wind’s authority and Fire’s function, and occupied the offices of the other gods as well. The gods were driven away, deprived of their realms and defeated.’
hindi: ‘उन्होंने वायु का अधिकार और अग्नि का कार्य भी अपने हाथ में लिया तथा अन्य देवताओं के पदों पर भी अधिकार कर लिया। तब देवता निकाल दिए गए, राज्यच्युत हुए और पराजित हो गए।’
note: The pinned line shifts between dual and singular forms; the surrounding narrative and comparison witness support Śumbha and Niśumbha as joint usurpers.

english: ‘All the gods, stripped of their authority and cast out by those two great asuras, remembered the undefeated Goddess.’
hindi: ‘उन दोनों महाअसुरों द्वारा अधिकारों से वंचित और निकाल दिए गए सभी देवताओं ने अपराजिता देवी का स्मरण किया।’
note: Aparājitā is translated as undefeated while preserving its role as a divine epithet.

english: ‘She had granted us this boon: “When remembered in times of danger, I shall destroy all your most terrible calamities that very moment.”’
hindi: ‘उन्होंने हमें यह वर दिया था: “आपत्ति में मेरा स्मरण किए जाने पर मैं उसी क्षण तुम्हारी सभी परम आपदाओं का नाश करूँगी।”’
note: The recalled boon is direct source speech and is not represented as a guaranteed outcome for every modern reciter.

english: Having resolved upon this, the gods went to Himavat, lord of mountains, and there offered full praise to the Goddess as Viṣṇumāyā.
hindi: ऐसा निश्चय करके देवता पर्वतराज हिमवान् के पास गए और वहाँ विष्णुमाया स्वरूप देवी की पूर्ण स्तुति की।
note: Viṣṇumāyā is retained as the source’s theological name rather than reduced to simple illusion.

english: The gods said: ‘Salutations to the Goddess, to the great Goddess; perpetual salutations to the auspicious one. Salutations to Prakṛti, to the gracious one; disciplined, we bow before her.’
hindi: देवताओं ने कहा: ‘देवी को नमस्कार, महादेवी को नमस्कार; शिवा को सदा नमस्कार। प्रकृति और भद्रा को नमस्कार; संयमित होकर हम उन्हें प्रणाम करते हैं।’
note: Śivā is rendered as the auspicious one; Prakṛti and Bhadrā remain source epithets.

english: ‘Salutations to the fierce one and the eternal one; salutations again and again to Gaurī and Dhātrī. Salutations to the Goddess who is the foundation of the world and to her who is action.’
hindi: ‘रौद्रा और नित्या को नमस्कार; गौरी और धात्री को बार-बार नमस्कार। जगत् की प्रतिष्ठा और क्रिया-स्वरूप देवी को बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned verse combines lines arranged differently in common recensions; every explicit epithet is translated in its observed order.

english: ‘Perpetual salutations to moonlight, to her whose form is the Moon, and to happiness. We bow again and again to the auspicious one, to growth for those who bow, and to accomplishment.’
hindi: ‘ज्योत्स्ना, चन्द्ररूपिणी और सुखस्वरूपा को सदा नमस्कार। कल्याणी, प्रणतों की वृद्धि और सिद्धि को बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned dyo-strā and case forms are irregular; jyotsnā, vṛddhi and siddhi are supported by parallel witnesses.

english: ‘Salutations again and again to Nairṛtī, to the prosperity of rulers and to Śarvāṇī; to Durgā, to the one who carries across difficulty, to the essence and the maker of all; and perpetual salutations to fame, to the dark one and the smoke-hued one.’
hindi: ‘नैरृती, राजाओं की लक्ष्मी और शर्वाणी को बार-बार नमस्कार; दुर्गा, दुर्ग से पार लगाने वाली, सारस्वरूपा और सर्वकारिणी को नमस्कार; ख्याति, कृष्णा और धूम्रवर्णा को सदा नमस्कार।’
note: This three-line pinned catalogue contains recension-sensitive epithets; Nairṛtī and Kṛṣṇā are retained rather than harmonized away.

english: ‘We bow to her who is exceedingly gentle and exceedingly fierce; salutations again and again. Salutations to the Goddess who is the foundation of the world and to her who is action.’
hindi: ‘जो अत्यन्त सौम्य और अत्यन्त रौद्र दोनों हैं, उन्हें हम प्रणाम करते हैं; बार-बार नमस्कार। जगत् की प्रतिष्ठा और क्रिया-स्वरूप देवी को बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned mano is treated as an orthographic error for namo; the second line repeats a formula already present in the observed verse 8.

english: ‘To the Goddess who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में विष्णुमाया कही जाती हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The repeated devotional refrain is translated literally; the manifestation remains source theology.

english: ‘To the Goddess who in all beings is called consciousness: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में चेतना कही जाती हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Cetanā is rendered as consciousness without asserting a modern theory of mind.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of intelligence: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में बुद्धि के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Buddhi is rendered as intelligence or discernment within the hymn’s manifestation formula.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of sleep: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में निद्रा के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned refrain has mano for namo in its final line; the repeated formula supports the correction in translation.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of hunger: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में क्षुधा के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The repeated devotional refrain is translated literally; it is not nutritional or health guidance.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of shadow: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में छाया के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Chāyā is kept as shadow rather than expanded into a later doctrinal system.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of power: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में शक्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Śakti is retained as power or energy within this specific refrain.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of thirst or craving: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में तृष्णा के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Tṛṣṇā can denote bodily thirst or craving; both senses remain available rather than being collapsed.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of forbearance: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में क्षान्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Kṣānti is rendered as forbearance or patience within the devotional formula.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of birth and distinctive kind: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में जाति अर्थात् जन्म और विशिष्ट प्रकार के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Jāti has metaphysical and classificatory senses here; it is not reduced to modern caste identity.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of modesty: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में लज्जा के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Lajjā is rendered as modesty without turning a historical virtue term into prescriptive gender conduct.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of peace: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में शान्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The repeated devotional refrain is translated literally.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of faith: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में श्रद्धा के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Śraddhā is retained as faith or trust within the source hymn.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of beauty and radiance: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में कान्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Kānti includes beauty, splendour and radiance; the English keeps both central senses.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of Lakṣmī and good fortune: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में लक्ष्मी के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Lakṣmī is retained as both divine name and good-fortune manifestation.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of steadfastness: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में धृति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned first refrain word tamas is treated as an orthographic error for namas; Pargiter notes dhṛti as edition-dependent while it is explicit here.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of activity and livelihood: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में वृत्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Vṛtti can mean activity, mode of being or livelihood; the translation preserves this semantic breadth.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of memory: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में स्मृति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Smṛti is translated as memory here, not as the separate textual genre unless context requires it.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of compassion: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में दया के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Dayā is rendered as compassion within the source hymn.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of right conduct and guidance: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में नीति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Nīti can denote conduct, policy or guidance; the pinned rūpeṇaṃ has an extra ending but the formula is clear.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of contentment: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में तुष्टि के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Tuṣṭi is rendered as contentment or satisfaction.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of nourishment and flourishing: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में पुष्टि के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Puṣṭi includes nourishment, thriving and fullness; Pargiter notes it as edition-dependent while it is explicit in this source.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of mother: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में मातृरूप से स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The maternal manifestation is source theology and is not used to reduce all feminine identities to motherhood.

english: ‘To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of error and bewilderment: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में भ्रान्ति के रूप में स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Bhrānti is translated as error or bewilderment without collapsing it into a medical diagnosis.

english: ‘To her who governs the senses of beings and is perpetually present in all beings—to that all-pervading Goddess, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो प्राणियों की इन्द्रियों की अधिष्ठात्री हैं और सभी भूतों में सदा व्याप्त हैं, उस व्याप्तिरूप देवी को बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: The pinned syntax is compressed around bhūtānāṃ and akhileṣu; governance of senses and pervasive presence are both preserved.

english: ‘To her who abides pervading this entire universe in the form of consciousness: salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations to her, salutations again and again.’
hindi: ‘जो इस सम्पूर्ण जगत् को चिति के रूप में व्याप्त करके स्थित हैं, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, उन्हें नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।’
note: Citi is retained in Hindi and rendered as consciousness in English; it is distinct from the earlier cetanā wording.

english: ‘May that sovereign Goddess, praised by the gods in former times when they sought their desired refuge and worshipped over many days by the lord of the gods, bring us auspicious and gracious things and strike down calamities.’
hindi: ‘पूर्वकाल में इच्छित आश्रय के लिए देवताओं द्वारा स्तुत और देवराज द्वारा अनेक दिनों तक सेवित वह ईश्वरी हमारे लिए शुभ और मंगलकारी फल करें तथा आपदाओं का नाश करें।’
note: The pinned sandhi tathāsurendreṇa is read as tathā surendreṇa, ‘and by the lord of the gods’; alternative segmentation would materially change the agent, so confidence is reduced.

english: ‘She whom we gods, now tormented by arrogant daityas, worship as sovereign, and who, when remembered by us with bodies bowed in devotion, destroys all our calamities that very moment—may she aid us.’
hindi: ‘उद्धत दैत्यों से पीड़ित हम देवता जिन्हें अभी ईश्वरी मानकर प्रणाम करते हैं और जिनका भक्तिपूर्वक झुके शरीर से स्मरण करने पर वे उसी क्षण हमारी सभी आपदाएँ हरती हैं—वे हमारी सहायता करें।’
note: The pinned final compound has an orthographic irregularity and difficult attachment; the translation follows the refrain’s petition without turning it into a universal guarantee.

english: The sage said: ‘While the gods were there engaged in hymns and other acts of praise, Pārvatī arrived to bathe in the waters of the Jāhnavī, O prince.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘हे राजकुमार, जब देवता वहाँ स्तुति आदि में लगे थे, तब पार्वती जाह्नवी के जल में स्नान करने आईं।’
note: Jāhnavī is retained as the source name for the Ganges.

english: The beautiful-browed Pārvatī asked the gods, ‘Whom are you praising here?’ Then the auspicious Goddess, emerging from the sheath of Pārvatī’s body, spoke.
hindi: सुन्दर भौंहों वाली पार्वती ने देवताओं से पूछा, ‘आप यहाँ किसकी स्तुति कर रहे हैं?’ तब पार्वती के शरीर-कोश से प्रकट हुई शिवा ने उत्तर दिया।
note: The pinned pronouns and speaker boundary are compressed; the comparison witness supports Pārvatī asking and the Goddess emerging from her bodily sheath to answer.

english: ‘This hymn to me is being offered by the assembled gods who were cast out by the daitya Śumbha and defeated in battle by Niśumbha.’
hindi: ‘यह मेरी स्तुति उन एकत्र देवताओं द्वारा की जा रही है जिन्हें दैत्य शुम्भ ने निकाल दिया और निशुम्भ ने युद्ध में पराजित किया।’
note: The response identifies the hymn’s addressee and the gods’ immediate grievance.

english: Because Ambikā issued forth from the bodily sheath of Pārvatī, she is therefore celebrated in all the worlds as Kauśikī.
hindi: पार्वती के शरीर-कोश से अम्बिका के निकलने के कारण वे सभी लोकों में कौशिकी नाम से गाई जाती हैं।
note: The source itself supplies the kośa-to-Kauśikī etymology; Devam preserves it as source etymology rather than modern philological proof.

english: When she had emerged, the remaining Pārvatī became dark and, taking refuge in the Himalaya, came to be known as Kālikā.
hindi: उनके निकल जाने पर शेष पार्वती कृष्णवर्णा हो गईं और हिमाचल में आश्रय लेकर कालिका नाम से प्रसिद्ध हुईं।
note: The verse’s identity relation between Kauśikī, Pārvatī and Kālikā is preserved without harmonizing all later theological traditions.

english: Then Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, servants of Śumbha and Niśumbha, saw Ambikā bearing a sublime and exceedingly captivating form.
hindi: तब शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के सेवक चण्ड और मुण्ड ने परम मनोहर रूप धारण किए अम्बिका को देखा।
note: The viewpoint now shifts to the two asura servants; their later report is not neutral narration.

english: They reported to Śumbha: ‘O great king, an indescribably beautiful woman is there, illuminating the Himalaya.’
hindi: उन दोनों ने शुम्भ से कहा: ‘हे महाराज, कोई अत्यन्त मनोहर स्त्री वहाँ हिमाचल को प्रकाशित करती हुई विराजमान है।’
note: This is Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa’s report within the narrative.

english: ‘No one anywhere has ever seen such surpassing beauty. Find out who this Goddess is and take possession of her, O lord of the asuras.’
hindi: ‘ऐसा उत्कृष्ट रूप किसी ने कहीं नहीं देखा। हे असुरेश्वर, पता लगाया जाए कि यह देवी कौन हैं और उन्हें अपने अधिकार में लिया जाए।’
note: The possessive command is translated explicitly as coercive character speech and is not endorsed by Devam.

english: ‘That jewel among women, of surpassingly beautiful form and illuminating the directions with her radiance, stands there, O lord of the daityas. You ought to see her.’
hindi: ‘अत्यन्त सुन्दर अंगों वाली, अपनी कान्ति से दिशाओं को प्रकाशित करती वह स्त्रीरत्न वहाँ खड़ी हैं, हे दैत्येन्द्र; आपको उन्हें देखना चाहिए।’
note: Strī-ratna is retained as the speakers’ objectifying comparison, not as Devam’s classification of women.

english: ‘O lord, all the treasures, jewels, elephants, horses and other valuables in the three worlds now shine in your house.’
hindi: ‘हे प्रभो, तीनों लोकों के सभी रत्न, मणियाँ, हाथी, घोड़े और अन्य मूल्यवान वस्तुएँ अब आपके घर में शोभित हैं।’
note: The catalogue is the servants’ boast about spoils seized by Śumbha, not a legitimate ownership claim.

english: ‘Airāvata, jewel among elephants, has been brought from Purandara; so too this Pārijāta tree and the horse Uccaiḥśravas.’
hindi: ‘हाथियों में रत्न ऐरावत पुरन्दर से लाया गया है; इसी प्रकार यह पारिजात वृक्ष और उच्चैःश्रवा घोड़ा भी।’
note: The source inventory presupposes seizure from Indra and is kept within the asuras’ boast.

english: ‘This swan-yoked aerial chariot stands in your courtyard—the wondrous jewel-like vehicle that once belonged to the Creator and was brought here.’
hindi: ‘हंसों से जुता यह विमान आपके आँगन में खड़ा है—वह अद्भुत रत्नमय वाहन जो पहले विधाता का था और यहाँ लाया गया।’
note: Vedhas is rendered as the Creator, conventionally Brahmā; vimāna remains a celestial vehicle in this source context.

english: ‘Here is the great treasure Mahāpadma, brought from the lord of wealth; and the Ocean gave the Kiñjalkinī garland of unfading lotuses.’
hindi: ‘यह महापद्म नामक निधि धनपति से लाई गई है और समुद्र ने कभी न मुरझाने वाले कमलों की किंजल्किनी माला दी है।’
note: Mahāpadma and Kiñjalkinī are retained as source names of the treasure and garland.

english: ‘Varuṇa’s umbrella, streaming gold, stands in your house; and here too is the finest chariot that formerly belonged to Prajāpati.’
hindi: ‘स्वर्ण बरसाने वाला वरुण का छत्र आपके घर में है और यह श्रेष्ठ रथ भी, जो पहले प्रजापति का था।’
note: Kāñcana-strāvi is rendered literally as streaming or showering gold; the item remains part of the boastful spoil catalogue.

english: ‘O lord, you took from Death the weapon called Utkrāntidā, the giver of departure; and your brother possesses the noose of the king of waters.’
hindi: ‘हे ईश, आपने मृत्यु से उत्क्रान्तिदा नामक शक्ति छीन ली और आपके भाई के अधिकार में जलराज का पाश है।’
note: Utkrāntidā is retained as a named weapon with a literal gloss; the Ocean-king or water-king is conventionally Varuṇa.

english: ‘All kinds of jewels born from the ocean belong to Niśumbha, and Fire himself gave you two garments purified by fire.’
hindi: ‘समुद्र से उत्पन्न सभी प्रकार के रत्न निशुम्भ के पास हैं और अग्नि ने आपको अग्निशुद्ध दो वस्त्र दिए।’
note: The pinned genitive construction is compact; comparison witnesses support Niśumbha as possessor of the ocean-born jewels.

english: ‘Thus, O lord of the daityas, you have taken every treasure. Why then do you not take this auspicious woman whom we call a jewel among women?’
hindi: ‘इस प्रकार हे दैत्येन्द्र, सभी रत्न आपने प्राप्त कर लिए हैं। फिर इस कल्याणमयी स्त्रीरत्न को आप अपने अधिकार में क्यों नहीं लेते?’
note: The verse completes the servants’ objectifying and coercive argument; Devam preserves it as antagonist speech.

english: The sage said: ‘After hearing these words of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the great asura Śumbha sent Sugrīva as a messenger to the Goddess.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘चण्ड और मुण्ड की यह बात सुनकर महाअसुर शुम्भ ने सुग्रीव को देवी के पास दूत बनाकर भेजा।’
note: Sugrīva here is Śumbha’s messenger in this episode, not automatically the Ramayana figure.

english: Śumbha said: ‘Go and speak to her in accordance with my words, saying this and that. Act deftly so that she comes here willingly and with pleasure.’
hindi: शुम्भ ने कहा: ‘जाकर मेरी आज्ञा के अनुसार उससे ये बातें कहना। ऐसा कौशल से करना कि वह प्रसन्नतापूर्वक यहाँ आ जाए।’
note: The pinned iti ceti ca is formulaic and irregular; the comparison witness supports a general instruction to deliver Śumbha’s message persuasively.

english: He went to the exceedingly beautiful place on the mountain where the Goddess was staying, and addressed her gently in a sweet voice.
hindi: वह पर्वत के उस अत्यन्त सुन्दर स्थान पर गया जहाँ देवी विराजमान थीं और मधुर वाणी में कोमलता से उनसे बोला।
note: The messenger’s pleasant manner is distinct from the coercive content that follows.

english: The messenger said: ‘O Goddess, Śumbha, lord of the daityas and supreme ruler of the three worlds, has sent me. I have come here into your presence as his messenger.’
hindi: दूत ने कहा: ‘हे देवी, तीनों लोकों का परम शासक दैत्येश्वर शुम्भ मुझे भेजकर आपके पास लाया है; मैं उसका दूत हूँ।’
note: Śumbha’s asserted universal sovereignty is character speech, not accepted narration.

english: ‘His command is never obstructed among any beings of divine origin, and he has vanquished every enemy of the daityas. Hear what he says.’
hindi: ‘सभी देवयोनियों में उसकी आज्ञा सदा निर्विघ्न चलती है और उसने दैत्यों के सभी शत्रुओं को जीत लिया है। अब उसका संदेश सुनो।’
note: The messenger’s claims of irresistible authority are reported, not authenticated facts outside the narrative.

english: ‘All three worlds are mine, and the gods obey my authority. I consume every share of every sacrifice separately.’
hindi: ‘सम्पूर्ण त्रैलोक्य मेरा है और देवता मेरे वश में हैं। मैं सभी यज्ञभागों को अलग-अलग ग्रहण करता हूँ।’
note: This is Śumbha’s boast relayed by the messenger.

english: ‘Every finest treasure in the three worlds is entirely under my control, including the jewel among elephants, the vehicle I took from the lord of the gods.’
hindi: ‘तीनों लोकों के सभी श्रेष्ठ रत्न पूर्णतः मेरे वश में हैं, और देवाधिपति का वाहन वह गजरत्न भी, जिसे मैंने छीन लिया।’
note: The sentence continues the messenger’s explicit admission of seizure.

english: ‘The immortals bowed and presented to me Uccaiḥśravas, that jewel among horses which arose from the churning of the Ocean of Milk.’
hindi: ‘क्षीरसागर-मन्थन से उत्पन्न उच्चैःश्रवा नामक अश्वरत्न देवताओं ने प्रणाम करके मुझे समर्पित किया।’
note: The messenger presents submission as voluntary; the larger narrative context records conquest and coercion.

english: ‘And whatever other beings regarded as treasures exist among the gods, gandharvas and nāgas—all of them are with me, O radiant one.’
hindi: ‘हे शोभने, देवताओं, गन्धर्वों और नागों के बीच जो अन्य रत्नरूप वस्तुएँ या प्राणी हैं, वे सब मेरे ही पास हैं।’
note: The source includes living beings in the rhetoric of possession; the translation preserves and contextualizes that objectification.

english: ‘O Goddess, we consider you the jewel among women in this world. Therefore come to us, for we are the enjoyers and possessors of treasures.’
hindi: ‘हे देवी, हम आपको संसार का स्त्रीरत्न मानते हैं। इसलिए हमारे पास आओ, क्योंकि हम रत्नों के भोक्ता और स्वामी हैं।’
note: This is the antagonist’s objectifying claim; Devam does not treat a person as transferable property.

english: ‘Choose me, or my younger brother Niśumbha of immense prowess, O lady of darting glances, since you are indeed a treasure.’
hindi: ‘हे चंचल नेत्रों वाली, मेरा या मेरे महापराक्रमी छोटे भाई निशुम्भ का वरण करो, क्योंकि तुम वास्तव में रत्न हो।’
note: Bhaj is rendered as choosing or accepting as partner in context; the messenger’s framing remains coercive and objectifying.

english: ‘By marrying me you will obtain incomparable supreme sovereignty. Consider this carefully and enter into marriage with me.’
hindi: ‘मुझसे विवाह करके तुम अनुपम परम ऐश्वर्य प्राप्त करोगी। इसे बुद्धिपूर्वक सोचकर मेरे साथ विवाह स्वीकार करो।’
note: The proposal’s promise of status is character persuasion, not Devam relationship advice.

english: The sage said: ‘Addressed in this way, the Goddess smiled deeply within and gave her reply—Durgā, the blessed and gracious one by whom this world is sustained.’
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: ‘इस प्रकार कहे जाने पर देवी ने भीतर ही गम्भीर मुस्कान की और उत्तर दिया—वे दुर्गा, भगवती और भद्रा, जिनसे यह जगत् धारण किया जाता है।’
note: Jagau literally ‘sang or spoke’ is rendered as gave her reply; the narrator’s theological epithets remain distinct from the messenger’s rhetoric.

english: The Goddess said: ‘You have spoken truly; nothing you have said here is false. Śumbha is lord of the three worlds, and Niśumbha is likewise powerful.’
hindi: देवी ने कहा: ‘तुमने सत्य कहा; यहाँ तुम्हारी कही कोई बात मिथ्या नहीं है। शुम्भ त्रैलोक्य का अधिपति है और निशुम्भ भी वैसा ही शक्तिशाली है।’
note: Her concession concerns their de facto power within the episode; it does not consent to the proposal.

english: ‘But how can what I have already vowed be made false? Hear the pledge that I once made in my lack of foresight.’
hindi: ‘किन्तु जो मैंने प्रतिज्ञा कर ली है, उसे मिथ्या कैसे किया जाए? सुनो, अल्पविचार के कारण मैंने पूर्वकाल में कौन-सी प्रतिज्ञा की थी।’
note: Alpa-buddhitva is rendered as lack of foresight rather than an enduring insult to the Goddess’s intelligence.

english: ‘He who conquers me in battle, who removes my pride and who is my equal in strength in this world—he shall become my husband.’
hindi: ‘जो मुझे संग्राम में जीते, मेरे गर्व को दूर करे और संसार में मेरे समान बलवान् हो, वही मेरा पति होगा।’
note: The vow establishes her explicit condition; it is not generalized into a relationship norm.

english: ‘Therefore let Śumbha come here, or the great asura Niśumbha. Let him defeat me and quickly take my hand—why delay?’
hindi: ‘अतः शुम्भ या महाअसुर निशुम्भ यहाँ आए। मुझे जीतकर शीघ्र मेरा पाणिग्रहण करे—अब विलम्ब क्यों?’
note: Pāṇi-grahaṇa is translated as taking the hand in marriage; consent remains conditioned on fulfilling her stated challenge.

english: The messenger said: ‘You are arrogant, Goddess. Do not speak this way before me. What man in the three worlds could stand before Śumbha and Niśumbha?’
hindi: दूत ने कहा: ‘हे देवी, तुम अभिमानी हो; मेरे सामने ऐसी बात मत कहो। तीनों लोकों में कौन पुरुष शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के सामने ठहर सकता है?’
note: The insult and challenge are the messenger’s speech, not narrator assessment.

english: ‘Even all the gods cannot face the other daityas in battle, O Goddess; how much less can you, a woman alone?’
hindi: ‘हे देवी, अन्य दैत्यों के सामने भी सभी देवता युद्ध में नहीं टिकते; फिर अकेली स्त्री होकर तुम कैसे टिकोगी?’
note: The misogynistic taunt is translated as antagonist speech and must not be retrieved as Devam guidance or a factual claim about women.

english: ‘Indra and all the other gods could not stand in battle against Śumbha and his allies. How then will you, a woman, go face them?’
hindi: ‘इन्द्र आदि सभी देवता शुम्भ और उसके साथियों के सामने युद्ध में नहीं टिक सके; तब स्त्री होकर तुम उनका सामना कैसे करोगी?’
note: This continues the messenger’s sexist intimidation and is explicitly scoped as character speech.

english: ‘Go, as I have told you, to the side of Śumbha and Niśumbha. Do not make yourself go there with your dignity shattered, dragged by the hair.’
hindi: ‘मेरी बात मानकर शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के पास चलो। ऐसा न हो कि केश पकड़कर घसीटे जाने से तुम्हारा गौरव नष्ट हो और तुम्हें वहाँ जाना पड़े।’
note: This is an explicit threat of coercive violence by the messenger; it must never be surfaced as acceptable conduct.

english: The Goddess said: ‘So it is: Śumbha is strong and Niśumbha immensely valiant. But what can I do? Long ago I made my pledge without fully considering it.’
hindi: देवी ने कहा: ‘ऐसा ही है—शुम्भ बलवान् और निशुम्भ अत्यन्त पराक्रमी है। किन्तु मैं क्या करूँ? मैंने पूर्वकाल में बिना पूरा विचार किए प्रतिज्ञा कर ली थी।’
note: Her ironic or strategic tone can be interpreted differently; the translation preserves the literal concession and pledge.

english: ‘Go now, and respectfully tell the lord of the asuras everything I have said to you. Let him then do what is fitting.’ Thus ends the eighty-fifth chapter in the Devī Māhātmya within the Sāvarṇika Manvantara of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.
hindi: ‘अब जाओ और मैंने जो कुछ तुमसे कहा है, वह सब आदरपूर्वक असुरराज को बताओ। फिर वह जो उचित समझे, करे।’ इस प्रकार श्रीमार्कण्डेयपुराण के सावर्णिक मन्वन्तर में देवीमाहात्म्य का पचासीवाँ अध्याय समाप्त हुआ।
note: The pinned colophon has severe joining irregularities and a provider phrase ‘next chapter’; those residues remain in the immutable source span but are not translated as sacred text.

english: The ṛṣi said: Hearing these words of the Goddess, the messenger, filled with indignation, returned and reported them fully to the daitya king.
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: देवी के ये वचन सुनकर वह दूत रोष से भर गया। लौटकर उसने दैत्यराज को पूरी बात विस्तार से सुनाई।
note: The messenger’s indignation is narrative description, not an endorsement of his response.

english: After hearing that statement from his messenger, the asura king became enraged and addressed Dhūmralocana, a commander of the daityas.
hindi: अपने दूत की वह बात सुनकर असुरराज क्रोधित हो उठा और उसने दैत्यों के सेनानायक धूम्रलोचन से कहा।
note: Adhipa may mean lord or commander here; the military narrative supports ‘commander’ without asserting a formal rank across editions.

english: ‘Dhūmralocana, go at once with your army around you. Bring that wicked woman here by force, distraught as she is dragged by the hair.’
hindi: ‘हे धूम्रलोचन, अपनी सेना से घिरकर शीघ्र जाओ। उस दुष्टा को बलपूर्वक यहाँ ले आओ, उसके केश खींचते हुए उसे व्याकुल कर दो।’
note: This is Śumbha’s abusive order and threat of coercive violence; it must never be surfaced as acceptable conduct or Devam guidance.

english: ‘If anyone else rises to protect her, he must be killed—whether a god, a yakṣa, or a gandharva.’
hindi: ‘यदि कोई दूसरा उसकी रक्षा के लिए उठ खड़ा हो, तो उसे भी मार डालना—चाहे वह देवता हो, यक्ष हो या गन्धर्व।’
note: The killing order remains explicitly attributed to the antagonist and is not a normative instruction.

english: The ṛṣi said: Thus commanded, the daitya Dhūmralocana set out at once, accompanied by sixty thousand asuras.
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: इस प्रकार आज्ञा पाकर दैत्य धूम्रलोचन साठ हजार असुरों से घिरा हुआ तत्काल चल पड़ा।
note: The number is retained literally as part of the epic battle narrative, not treated as independently historical enumeration.

english: Seeing the Goddess stationed on the snowy mountain, he called out loudly, ‘Go to the presence of Śumbha and Niśumbha!’
hindi: हिमाचल पर स्थित देवी को देखकर उसने ऊँचे स्वर में कहा, ‘शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के समक्ष चलो!’
note: Mūlam is rendered contextually as ‘the presence’; readings such as camp, headquarters, or side remain possible.

english: ‘If you will not willingly go to my lord today, I will take you by force, leaving you distraught as you are dragged by the hair.’
hindi: ‘यदि आज तुम अपनी इच्छा से मेरे स्वामी के पास नहीं चलोगी, तो मैं तुम्हें बलपूर्वक ले जाऊँगा और केश पकड़कर घसीटते हुए व्याकुल कर दूँगा।’
note: This is Dhūmralocana’s explicit threat of abduction and violence, preserved as antagonist speech and barred from guidance use.

english: The Goddess said: ‘Sent by the lord of the daityas, you are powerful and surrounded by an army. If you carry me away by force like this, what then can I do to you?’
hindi: देवी ने कहा: ‘तुम्हें दैत्यराज ने भेजा है; तुम बलवान् हो और सेना से घिरे हो। यदि तुम मुझे इस प्रकार बलपूर्वक ले जाते हो, तो मैं तुम्हारा क्या कर सकती हूँ?’
note: Her response may be read as ironic or strategic; the translation preserves its literal rhetorical form without deciding the tone.

english: The ṛṣi said: Thus addressed, the asura Dhūmralocana rushed at her. Ambikā then reduced him to ashes with a single sound of hūṃ.
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: यह सुनकर असुर धूम्रलोचन उनकी ओर दौड़ा। तब अम्बिका ने केवल एक ‘हुँ’ की ध्वनि से उसे भस्म कर दिया।
note: Hūṃkāra is kept as the specific uttered sound rather than generalized into an ordinary shout or a user-prescribed mantra.

english: Then Ambikā showered the enraged great army of the asuras with sharp arrows, spears, and axes.
hindi: तब अम्बिका ने असुरों की उस क्रुद्ध विशाल सेना पर तीखे बाणों, शक्तियों और फरसों की वर्षा कर दी।
note: The pinned source reads Ambikā in the nominative and makes her the subject; Pargiter’s comparison witness instead makes the army shower Ambikā, so the syntactic variant is preserved as material uncertainty.

english: Then the Goddess’s lion, her mount, shook his mane in fury, gave a terrifying roar, and sprang upon the asura army.
hindi: तब देवी का वाहन सिंह क्रोध से अपनी अयाल झटकता हुआ अत्यन्त भयानक गर्जना करके असुर-सेना पर टूट पड़ा।
note: The martial violence is retained as episode-specific narrative and not generalized into devotional instruction.

english: He killed some daityas with blows of his paws, others with his mouth, and still other great asuras by crushing them beneath him.
hindi: उसने कुछ दैत्यों को पंजों के प्रहार से, कुछ को अपने मुख से और अन्य महासुरों को अपने नीचे दबाकर मार डाला।
note: Adhareṇa literally invokes a lower part and has variant renderings; ‘crushing them beneath him’ preserves the action without inventing a precise limb.

english: With his claws the lion tore open the bellies of some; with blows of his paw he struck the heads of others apart.
hindi: सिंह ने कुछ के पेट अपने नखों से चीर दिए और पंजे के प्रहार से दूसरों के सिर धड़ से अलग कर दिए।
note: The source’s spelling talaprihāreṇa is treated as the expected talaprahāreṇa sense, while the immutable Sanskrit remains unchanged.

english: Others fell with their arms and heads severed by him; and, shaking his mane, he drank the blood from the bellies of still others.
hindi: अन्य असुर उसके द्वारा भुजाएँ और सिर काट दिए जाने पर गिर पड़े; और अयाल झटकते हुए उसने कुछ अन्य के पेटों से बहता रक्त पी लिया।
note: The compact form sṛtās is rendered from context as falling or going down; the source’s grammatical irregularity remains disclosed.

english: In a moment that entire force was brought to destruction by the great-hearted lion, the Goddess’s mount, who was fiercely enraged.
hindi: क्षणभर में देवी के वाहन उस महात्मा और अत्यन्त क्रुद्ध सिंह ने उस पूरी सेना का विनाश कर दिया।
note: Mahātman is rendered as ‘great-hearted’ within epic praise and is not an independently evaluative claim about violence.

english: Then Śumbha heard that the Goddess had slain the asura Dhūmralocana and that her lion had destroyed his entire force.
hindi: तब शुम्भ ने सुना कि देवी ने असुर धूम्रलोचन को मार डाला और देवी के सिंह ने उसकी पूरी सेना का संहार कर दिया।
note: The pinned form kṛtstraṃ is understood as the expected kṛtsnaṃ, ‘entire’; the source spelling is not silently altered.

english: The daitya lord Śumbha became enraged, his lip quivering, and commanded the two great asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
hindi: दैत्यराज शुम्भ क्रोध से भर उठा; उसका होंठ फड़कने लगा और उसने उन दोनों महासुरों चण्ड और मुण्ड को आज्ञा दी।
note: The physical detail marks Śumbha’s anger within the narrative and carries no diagnostic meaning.

english: ‘Caṇḍa, Muṇḍa—go there surrounded by numerous forces. Once there, bring her here quickly.’
hindi: ‘हे चण्ड, हे मुण्ड, बहुत-सी सेनाओं से घिरे हुए वहाँ जाओ। वहाँ पहुँचकर उसे शीघ्र यहाँ ले आओ।’
note: The abduction order is antagonist speech and must not be detached from its narrative attribution.

english: ‘Drag her by the hair or bind her. If you have any doubt in battle, let all the asuras strike her down with every weapon.’
hindi: ‘उसके केश पकड़कर घसीटो या उसे बाँध लो। यदि युद्ध में तुम्हें कोई संशय हो, तो सभी असुर अपने समस्त शस्त्रों से उसे मार डालें।’
note: This continues Śumbha’s coercive and lethal order; it is preserved solely as attributed antagonist speech.

english: ‘When that wicked woman has been killed and her lion struck down, return quickly after binding and seizing Ambikā.’ Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, named ‘The Slaying of Dhūmralocana,’ in the Devī Māhātmya within the Sāvarṇika Manvantara of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Mahāpurāṇa.
hindi: ‘उस दुष्टा के मारे जाने और उसके सिंह के गिरा दिए जाने पर अम्बिका को बाँधकर पकड़ लो और शीघ्र लौट आओ।’ इस प्रकार श्रीमार्कण्डेयमहापुराण के सावर्णिक मन्वन्तर में देवीमाहात्म्य का ‘धूम्रलोचन-वध’ नामक छियासीवाँ अध्याय समाप्त हुआ।
note: The command’s tension between killing her and then bringing her bound is retained rather than harmonized; the trailing provider notation ‘87(84)’ is an editorial residue, not translated sacred text.

english: The ṛṣi said: Thus commanded, the daityas led by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa set out with weapons raised and a fourfold army.
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: इस प्रकार आज्ञा पाकर चण्ड और मुण्ड के नेतृत्व में दैत्य उठे हुए शस्त्रों तथा चतुरंगिणी सेना के साथ चल पड़े।
note: The fourfold army conventionally comprises infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants; the translation does not add those unstated components to the source text.

english: They then saw the Goddess, faintly smiling, seated upon the lion on a great golden peak of the lord of mountains.
hindi: तब उन्होंने देवी को मंद मुस्कान के साथ सिंह पर विराजमान देखा; वे पर्वतराज के एक विशाल स्वर्णिम शिखर पर स्थित थीं।
note: The mountain is described through the epithet ‘lord of mountains’; identification beyond the episode’s Himalayan setting is not expanded here.

english: On seeing her, they prepared to seize her; some advanced close with bows drawn and swords in hand.
hindi: उन्हें देखकर वे देवी को पकड़ने के लिए उद्यत हुए; कुछ धनुष चढ़ाए और तलवारें लिए उनके निकट बढ़ आए।
note: The pinned compound near the close is irregular; the translation follows the coherent approach-and-capture sense also supported by the comparison witness.

english: Then Ambikā became intensely angry with those enemies, and in her anger her face turned the colour of ink.
hindi: तब उन शत्रुओं पर अम्बिका का क्रोध अत्यन्त प्रबल हो उठा और क्रोध से उनका मुख स्याही के समान काला हो गया।
note: The colour transformation belongs to the episode’s divine manifestation and is not generalized into human emotion or physiology.

english: From the surface of her forehead, curved by a frown, Kālī suddenly emerged—terrible-faced and bearing a sword and noose.
hindi: भृकुटि से वक्र हुई उनकी ललाट-भूमि से सहसा विकराल मुखवाली, तलवार और पाश धारण किए काली प्रकट हुईं।
note: Kālī is presented here through this specific manifestation narrative; the row does not settle every theological account of her identity.

english: She bore a many-coloured khaṭvāṅga, was adorned with a garland of human heads, wore a leopard skin, and was exceedingly terrifying with her emaciated flesh.
hindi: वे विचित्र खट्वाङ्ग धारण किए थीं, नर-मुण्डों की माला से विभूषित थीं, चीते की खाल पहने थीं और सूखे मांस वाले शरीर के कारण अत्यन्त भयंकर दिखती थीं।
note: Dvīpin can denote leopard or tiger in transmission; ‘leopard’ follows the direct lexical reading while the source image remains visible for comparison.

english: Her mouth was immensely wide, her lolling tongue terrifying, her red eyes deep-set, and her roar filled every direction.
hindi: उनका मुख अत्यन्त विशाल था, लपलपाती जिह्वा भयंकर थी, लाल नेत्र भीतर धँसे हुए थे और उनकी गर्जना से सभी दिशाएँ भर गईं।
note: The fierce iconographic description is kept episode-specific and does not exhaust later Kālī traditions or visual conventions.

english: She rushed forward with force, slaying the great asuras, and there in the army of the gods’ enemies she devoured that force.
hindi: वे वेग से आगे बढ़ीं, महासुरों का वध करती हुईं, और देवताओं के शत्रुओं की उस सेना में उनके बल को निगलने लगीं।
note: The graphic battle action is sacred narrative, not a ritual prescription or a general moral instruction.

english: With one hand she seized elephants together with their rear riders, goadsmen, warriors, and bells, and flung them into her mouth.
hindi: उन्होंने एक ही हाथ से हाथियों को उनके पीछे बैठे सहायकों, अंकुशधारी चालकों, योद्धाओं और घंटियों सहित उठाकर अपने मुख में फेंक दिया।
note: The compact elephant-crew compounds permit different role labels; all named components are retained without claiming a standardized crew structure.

english: Likewise she cast warriors with their horses and chariots with their drivers into her mouth, grinding them terribly with her teeth.
hindi: इसी प्रकार उन्होंने योद्धाओं को उनके घोड़ों सहित और रथों को सारथियों सहित मुख में डालकर दाँतों से अत्यन्त भयानक रूप से चबा डाला।
note: The source’s compressed coordination is expanded only enough for readable English and Hindi; no additional battle units are inferred.

english: She seized one by the hair and another by the neck, crushed another beneath her foot, and pounded yet another against her breast.
hindi: उन्होंने एक को केशों से और दूसरे को गर्दन से पकड़ा, एक अन्य को पैर के नीचे दबाया और दूसरे को वक्ष से कुचल दिया।
note: The sequence is translated literally as graphic episode action and must not be detached into behavioural guidance.

english: In fury she caught in her mouth the weapons and great missiles released by the asuras and crushed them with her teeth.
hindi: असुरों द्वारा छोड़े गए शस्त्रों और महास्त्रों को उन्होंने क्रोध में अपने मुख से पकड़ लिया और दाँतों से चूर कर दिया।
note: The pinned spelling śastraṇi is understood as śastrāṇi; the immutable source remains uncorrected.

english: She crushed the entire force of those powerful, wicked asuras; she devoured some and struck down others.
hindi: उन्होंने उन बलवान् दुरात्मा असुरों की पूरी सेना को कुचल दिया; कुछ को निगल लिया और दूसरों को प्रहार करके गिरा दिया।
note: The narrator’s epithet ‘wicked’ is retained as episode characterization, not converted into a general label for human opponents.

english: Some asuras were slain by her sword, some battered by her khaṭvāṅga, and others perished in battle when struck by the tips of her teeth.
hindi: कुछ असुर उनकी तलवार से मारे गए, कुछ खट्वाङ्ग के प्रहार से और अन्य युद्ध में उनके दाँतों की नोक से घायल होकर नष्ट हुए।
note: Khaṭvāṅga is preserved as the named weapon rather than flattened into a generic club.

english: Seeing that great asura army felled in an instant, Caṇḍa rushed at the terrifying Kālī.
hindi: उस विशाल असुर-सेना को क्षणभर में धराशायी देखकर चण्ड उस अत्यन्त भयंकर काली की ओर दौड़ा।
note: The pinned second half is textually corrupt; the translation follows the recoverable Caṇḍa-rushes-at-Kālī reading supported by the comparison witness, while the uncertainty remains explicit.

english: The great asura covered the terrible-eyed Goddess with fearsome showers of arrows, while Muṇḍa covered her with thousands of hurled discuses.
hindi: महासुर ने उन भयंकर नेत्रोंवाली देवी को विकराल बाण-वर्षा से ढक दिया और मुण्ड ने हजारों चक्र फेंककर उन्हें आच्छादित कर दिया।
note: The first attacker is supplied by continuity from Caṇḍa in the corrupt preceding row; Muṇḍa is explicit in the second half, so the two attacks remain distinct.

english: The many discuses entering her mouth shone like a multitude of solar orbs entering the body of a cloud.
hindi: उनके मुख में प्रवेश करते वे अनेक चक्र ऐसे चमक रहे थे मानो बहुत-से सूर्यमण्डल किसी मेघ के गर्भ में प्रवेश कर रहे हों।
note: The simile is preserved without turning the battle image into a cosmological assertion.

english: Then Kālī, roaring terribly, laughed fearsomely in extreme fury, the dreadful teeth within her terrible mouth blazing into view.
hindi: तब भयंकर गर्जना करती काली ने प्रचण्ड क्रोध में विकराल अट्टहास किया; उनके कराल मुख के भीतर दुर्दर्श दाँत चमक उठे।
note: The fierce laughter and appearance are attributes of this battle manifestation, not a complete iconographic prescription.

english: Mounting the great lion, the Goddess rushed at Caṇḍa, seized him by the hair, and cut off his head with her sword.
hindi: महान् सिंह पर चढ़कर देवी चण्ड की ओर दौड़ीं, उसके केश पकड़ लिए और अपनी तलवार से उसका सिर काट दिया।
note: The pinned verb form is irregular; the mounting-and-rushing sense is supported by the narrative and comparison witness without changing the source bytes.

english: When the head was severed, the lord of the daityas gave a terrifying cry; that mighty sound frightened the three worlds.
hindi: सिर कटते ही दैत्येन्द्र ने अत्यन्त भयानक चीत्कार किया; उस महान् नाद से तीनों लोक भयभीत हो गए।
note: This extra cry verse is present in the pinned 26-verse provider revision but absent from Pargiter’s 25-verse comparison sequence; the identity of ‘lord of the daityas’ is not silently resolved.

english: Then, seeing Caṇḍa fallen, Muṇḍa rushed at her. In fury she struck him with her sword and felled him to the ground as well.
hindi: चण्ड को गिरा हुआ देखकर मुण्ड भी उनकी ओर दौड़ा। उन्होंने क्रोध में तलवार का प्रहार करके उसे भी भूमि पर गिरा दिया।
note: The verse states the battle sequence without adding a theological interpretation of the deaths.

english: Seeing Caṇḍa fallen and the immensely valiant Muṇḍa slain, the surviving army fled in terror in every direction.
hindi: चण्ड को गिरा और अत्यन्त पराक्रमी मुण्ड को मारा हुआ देखकर बची हुई सेना भय से व्याकुल होकर सभी दिशाओं में भाग गई।
note: The compact syntax is resolved through the immediately preceding deaths; no independent historical battle claim is made.

english: Taking the heads of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, Kālī approached Caṇḍikā and spoke amid fierce, resounding laughter.
hindi: चण्ड और मुण्ड के सिर लेकर काली चण्डिका के पास पहुँचीं और प्रचण्ड अट्टहास के बीच बोलीं।
note: The second ‘head’ is elliptical in the pinned Sanskrit and supplied from the parallel construction and episode context.

english: ‘Here I have brought you Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, two great sacrificial beasts. In this battle-sacrifice you yourself will slay Śumbha and Niśumbha.’
hindi: ‘यहाँ मैं तुम्हारे लिए चण्ड और मुण्ड—इन दो महापशुओं—को ले आई हूँ। इस युद्ध-यज्ञ में शुम्भ और निशुम्भ का वध तुम स्वयं करोगी।’
note: The verse uses an explicit battle-as-sacrifice metaphor; it is literary theology, not authorization for sacrifice or violence in practice.

english: The ṛṣi said: Seeing the two great asuras Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa brought before her, the auspicious Caṇḍikā spoke these gracious words to Kālī.
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: उन दोनों महासुरों चण्ड और मुण्ड को अपने सामने लाया हुआ देखकर कल्याणमयी चण्डिका ने काली से ये मधुर वचन कहे।
note: Lalita is rendered as gracious or gentle in the contrastive speech setting, not as a separate identity claim.

english: The Goddess said: ‘Because you came after seizing Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, O Goddess, you will henceforth be renowned in the world as Cāmuṇḍā.’ Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter, named ‘The Slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa,’ in the Devī Māhātmya within the Sāvarṇika Manvantara of the Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa.
hindi: देवी ने कहा: ‘हे देवि, क्योंकि तुम चण्ड और मुण्ड को पकड़कर यहाँ आई हो, इसलिए अब संसार में तुम चामुण्डा नाम से प्रसिद्ध होगी।’ इस प्रकार श्रीमार्कण्डेयपुराण के सावर्णिक मन्वन्तर में देवीमाहात्म्य का ‘चण्ड-मुण्ड-वध’ नामक सत्तासीवाँ अध्याय समाप्त हुआ।
note: This verse gives the episode’s Cāmuṇḍā naming etiology; it does not erase other textual or living traditions of Cāmuṇḍā. The trailing provider notation ‘88(85)’ is editorial residue.

english: The ṛṣi said: When the daitya Caṇḍa had been slain, Muṇḍa struck down, and many armies destroyed, the lord of the asuras—
hindi: ऋषि ने कहा: दैत्य चण्ड के मारे जाने, मुण्ड के गिरा दिए जाने और अनेक सेनाओं के नष्ट हो जाने पर असुरों का स्वामी—
note: The sentence deliberately continues into the next verse; the dash preserves that source segmentation rather than inventing a complete claim.

english: —the mighty Śumbha, his mind overcome by anger, ordered the mobilization of all the daitya forces.
hindi: —वह प्रतापी शुम्भ, जिसका मन क्रोध के वश में था, समस्त दैत्य-सेनाओं को युद्ध के लिए तैयार होने की आज्ञा देने लगा।
note: This completes the syntax begun in verse 1 while keeping the two source citations separately addressable.

english: ‘Today let the eighty-six daitya contingents march with all their forces and weapons raised; let the eighty-four Kambus set out, each surrounded by its own force.’
hindi: ‘आज छियासी दैत्य-दल अपनी समस्त सेना और उठे हुए शस्त्रों के साथ चलें; चौरासी कम्बु-दल भी अपनी-अपनी सेनाओं से घिरे हुए प्रस्थान करें।’
note: The transmitted numbers and Kambu name are retained, but the exact historical or genealogical unit denoted by each count remains uncertain.

english: ‘Let the fifty clans of the asuras called Koṭivīrya and the hundred clans of the Dhaumras march out at my command.’
hindi: ‘कोटिवीर्य नामक असुरों के पचास कुल और धौम्रों के सौ कुल मेरी आज्ञा से निकल पड़ें।’
note: Koṭivīrya and Dhaumra are preserved as transmitted group names; the verse is not independent evidence for historical population counts.

english: ‘Let the Kālakas, Daurhṛdas, Mauryas, and Kālakeya asuras hasten out at my command, ready for battle.’
hindi: ‘कालक, दौर्हृद, मौर्य और कालकेय असुर मेरी आज्ञा से शीघ्र युद्ध के लिए तैयार होकर निकलें।’
note: The proper names vary across witnesses; this row transliterates the pinned forms and does not equate them with later historical dynasties.

english: Having issued these commands, Śumbha, the asura lord whose rule was terrifying, set out surrounded by many thousands of great troops.
hindi: ये आज्ञाएँ देकर भयंकर शासन वाला असुरपति शुम्भ अनेक हजार विशाल सैन्य-दलों से घिरा हुआ निकल पड़ा।
note: ‘Terrifying rule’ renders bhairava-śāsana as an episode epithet, not a political-historical assessment.

english: Seeing that exceedingly terrible army approaching, Caṇḍikā filled the space between earth and sky with the twang of her bowstring.
hindi: उस अत्यन्त भयंकर सेना को आते देखकर चण्डिका ने अपने धनुष की प्रत्यञ्चा की टंकार से पृथ्वी और आकाश के बीच का अन्तर भर दिया।
note: The cosmic-scale acoustics belong to the epic narration and are not treated as physically measured sound.

english: Her lion gave an exceedingly great roar, O king, and Ambikā amplified that sound with the ringing of her bell.
hindi: हे राजन्, उनके सिंह ने अत्यन्त प्रचण्ड गर्जना की और अम्बिका ने अपनी घंटा-ध्वनि से उस नाद को और बढ़ा दिया।
note: The direct address to the king is retained as part of the frame narration.

english: As every direction filled with the sounds of bowstring, lion, and bell, Kālī opened her mouth wide and surpassed them with terrifying cries.
hindi: धनुष की प्रत्यञ्चा, सिंह और घंटा के नाद से सभी दिशाएँ भर गईं; काली ने मुख फैलाकर अपनी भयानक गर्जनाओं से उन सब ध्वनियों को पीछे छोड़ दिया।
note: Jigye is read as ‘surpassed’ in the contest of sounds; alternative syntactic readings remain possible.

english: Hearing that sound, the enraged daitya armies surrounded the Goddess, her lion, and Kālī from all four directions.
hindi: उस नाद को सुनकर क्रुद्ध दैत्य-सेनाओं ने चारों दिशाओं से देवी, उनके सिंह और काली को घेर लिया।
note: The source coordination is compact; the three surrounded figures are preserved without merging Kālī into an unqualified identity equation.

english: At that moment, O king, for the destruction of the gods’ enemies and the welfare of the lion-like immortals, powers endowed with immense strength and valour—
hindi: उसी समय, हे राजन्, देवताओं के शत्रुओं के विनाश और सिंह-समान अमरों के कल्याण के लिए अत्यन्त पराक्रम और बल से सम्पन्न शक्तियाँ—
note: The sentence continues into verse 12. Provider-inserted thumbnail captions in the immutable span are non-scriptural interface residue and are not translated.

english: —emerged from the bodies of Brahmā, Īśa, Guha, Viṣṇu, and Indra, assumed their corresponding forms, and came to Caṇḍikā.
hindi: —ब्रह्मा, ईश, गुह, विष्णु और इन्द्र के शरीरों से निकलीं, उन्हीं के अनुरूप रूप धारण करके चण्डिका के पास आईं।
note: These are the episode’s deity-power manifestations; the row does not settle every Śākta doctrine concerning ontological dependence or identity.

english: Whatever the form, ornaments, and vehicle of each god, in just that appearance his śakti came to battle the asuras.
hindi: जिस देवता का जैसा रूप, आभूषण और वाहन था, उसी के अनुरूप उसकी शक्ति असुरों से युद्ध करने आई।
note: Śakti is preserved as a technical term whose theological scope exceeds the English word ‘power’.

english: At the front of a celestial vehicle drawn by swans came Brahmā’s śakti, carrying a rosary and water pot; she is called Brahmāṇī.
hindi: हंसों से जुते दिव्य विमान के अग्रभाग में ब्रह्मा की शक्ति अक्षमाला और कमण्डलु लिए आईं; वे ब्रह्माणी कहलाती हैं।
note: The naming and iconography are bound to this witness and do not replace wider Mātṛkā traditions.

english: Māheśvarī arrived mounted on a bull, bearing an excellent trident, wearing great serpents as ornaments, and adorned with the crescent moon.
hindi: माहेश्वरी वृषभ पर आरूढ़ होकर आईं; वे उत्तम त्रिशूल धारण किए, विशाल सर्पों के आभूषण पहने और चन्द्रकला से विभूषित थीं।
note: The compact serpent compound may denote bracelets or encircling ornaments; the translation keeps the broader ornament sense.

english: Kaumārī, Ambikā in Guha’s form, approached to battle the daityas, spear in hand and riding a splendid peacock.
hindi: गुह के रूपवाली अम्बिका कौमारी हाथ में शक्ति लिए और श्रेष्ठ मयूर पर आरूढ़ होकर दैत्यों से युद्ध करने आईं।
note: The verse’s Guha-form relation is preserved without collapsing all uses of Ambikā, Kaumārī, and the supreme Goddess into one universal taxonomy.

english: Likewise Vaiṣṇavī śakti came seated upon Garuḍa, holding conch, discus, mace, Śārṅga bow, and sword.
hindi: इसी प्रकार वैष्णवी शक्ति गरुड़ पर स्थित होकर आईं; उनके हाथों में शंख, चक्र, गदा, शार्ङ्ग धनुष और तलवार थे।
note: Śārṅga is retained as the named bow rather than translated generically.

english: The śakti bearing Hari’s incomparable boar form also came there, assuming the body of Vārāhī.
hindi: हरि के अनुपम वराह-रूप को धारण करनेवाली शक्ति भी वाराही का शरीर लेकर वहाँ आईं।
note: The pinned syntax is irregular, but the Vārāhī manifestation is clear and independently coherent within the surrounding sequence.

english: Nārasiṃhī arrived bearing a body like Nṛsiṃha’s, the tossing of her mane scattering clusters of stars.
hindi: नृसिंह के समान शरीर धारण किए नारसिंही वहाँ आईं; उनकी अयाल के झटकों से नक्षत्र-समूह बिखर रहे थे।
note: The star-scattering image is epic cosmological poetry, not an astronomical claim.

english: Aindrī likewise arrived seated upon the lord of elephants, thunderbolt in hand and thousand-eyed—just as Śakra is, so was she.
hindi: इसी प्रकार ऐन्द्री गजराज पर स्थित होकर, हाथ में वज्र और सहस्र नेत्रों सहित आईं; जैसी आकृति शक्र की थी, वैसी ही उनकी थी।
note: The likeness formula is local to this śakti manifestation and does not resolve broader Indrāṇī traditions.

english: Then Īśāna, surrounded by those divine śaktis, said to Caṇḍikā, ‘Let the asuras be slain quickly for my satisfaction.’
hindi: तब उन देवशक्तियों से घिरे ईशान ने चण्डिका से कहा, ‘मेरी प्रसन्नता के लिए असुरों का शीघ्र वध हो।’
note: The speaker and agency are preserved as transmitted; this divine battle speech is not a human authorization for violence.

english: Then from the Goddess’s body emerged Caṇḍikā’s śakti, exceedingly fierce and terrifying, howling like a hundred jackals.
hindi: तब देवी के शरीर से चण्डिका की अत्यन्त उग्र और भयंकर शक्ति प्रकट हुई, जिसकी ध्वनि सौ सियारों के नाद जैसी थी।
note: The pinned opening compound is irregular and read as ‘from the Goddess’s body’ through the coherent manifestation sequence; no user practice is inferred from the jackal image.

english: She, the unconquered one, said to smoke-hued, matted-haired Īśāna, ‘Blessed lord, go as my messenger to Śumbha and Niśumbha.’
hindi: उस अपराजिता ने धूम्रवर्ण और जटाधारी ईशान से कहा, ‘भगवन्, तुम मेरे दूत बनकर शुम्भ और निशुम्भ के पास जाओ।’
note: Aparājitā functions as an epithet here; the row does not assert that every textual Aparājitā identity is identical.

english: ‘Tell the exceedingly arrogant dānavas Śumbha and Niśumbha, and the other dānavas assembled there for battle—’
hindi: ‘अत्यन्त गर्वित दानव शुम्भ और निशुम्भ से तथा वहाँ युद्ध के लिए उपस्थित अन्य दानवों से कहो—’
note: The sentence continues into the ultimatum in verse 25; the attribution remains the Goddess’s message.

english: ‘Let Indra regain the three worlds and the gods receive the sacrificial offerings. If you wish to live, go down to Pātāla.’
hindi: ‘इन्द्र को तीनों लोक पुनः मिलें और देवता हवि के भोक्ता हों। यदि तुम जीवित रहना चाहते हो, तो पाताल चले जाओ।’
note: This is an ultimatum within the mythic sovereignty conflict, not a geographical or ritual instruction.

english: ‘But if, proud of your strength, you desire battle, then come—let my jackals be glutted with your flesh.’
hindi: ‘किन्तु यदि अपने बल के गर्व में तुम युद्ध चाहते हो, तो आओ; मेरे सियार तुम्हारे मांस से तृप्त हों।’
note: The threat and flesh imagery are divine battle speech, explicitly barred from extraction as normative guidance or ritual practice.

english: Because the Goddess herself appointed Śiva to the work of a messenger, she thereby became renowned in this world as Śivadūtī.
hindi: क्योंकि देवी ने स्वयं शिव को दूत-कार्य में नियुक्त किया था, इसलिए वे इस संसार में शिवदूती नाम से प्रसिद्ध हुईं।
note: This is the episode’s Śivadūtī naming etiology and does not exhaust other Śivadūtī texts, forms, or traditions.

english: Hearing the Goddess’s message reported by Śarva, those great asuras were filled with indignation and went to where Kātyāyanī stood.
hindi: शर्व द्वारा सुनाया गया देवी का संदेश सुनकर वे महासुर रोष से भर गए और जहाँ कात्यायनी स्थित थीं वहाँ जा पहुँचे।
note: Śarva and Kātyāyanī are preserved as contextual names; the passage does not establish universal equivalence rules among divine names.

english: At once, the gods’ enemies at the front, swollen with indignation, showered the Goddess with arrows, spears, and lances.
hindi: तुरन्त अग्रभाग में स्थित देव-शत्रुओं ने उग्र रोष से देवी पर बाणों, शक्तियों और ऋष्टियों की वर्षा कर दी।
note: The weapon terms retain distinct source categories; their exact material forms may differ across martial lexicons.

english: With effortless skill she cut apart the hurled arrows, tridents, spears, and axes using great shafts released from her resounding bow.
hindi: उन्होंने अपने गूँजते धनुष से छोड़े गए महान् बाणों द्वारा उन फेंके हुए बाणों, शूलों, शक्तियों और फरसों को खेल-खेल में काट दिया।
note: Ādhmāta is rendered through the comparison-supported resounding-bow sense; the source does not imply literal inflation of the bow.

english: Before her, Kālī moved through the battle, tearing enemies apart with descending trident blows and crushing them with her khaṭvāṅga.
hindi: उनके आगे काली युद्धभूमि में घूमती हुई शूल-प्रहारों से शत्रुओं को चीरती और खट्वाङ्ग से कुचलती रहीं।
note: The source’s passive-result compounds are rendered as Kālī’s ongoing battle action; the violence remains episode-specific.

english: Wherever Brahmāṇī moved, she cast water from her water pot upon the enemies, draining their valour and strength.
hindi: ब्रह्माणी जहाँ-जहाँ गईं, वहाँ कमण्डलु का जल शत्रुओं पर छिड़ककर उनके पराक्रम और तेज को क्षीण करती गईं।
note: This divine battle effect is not converted into a claim that ordinary water or a user ritual has the same power.

english: Māheśvarī slew daityas with her trident, Vaiṣṇavī with her discus, and the fiercely enraged Kaumārī with her spear.
hindi: माहेश्वरी ने त्रिशूल से, वैष्णवी ने चक्र से और अत्यन्त क्रुद्ध कौमारी ने शक्ति से दैत्यों का वध किया।
note: Each weapon-action pairing remains attached to this chapter’s manifestation sequence.

english: Struck and torn apart by Aindrī’s thunderbolt, daityas and dānavas fell to the earth by the hundreds, pouring streams of blood.
hindi: ऐन्द्री के वज्र-प्रहार से विदीर्ण होकर सैकड़ों दैत्य और दानव रक्त की धाराएँ बहाते हुए पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े।
note: The large-scale and graphic battle description is not treated as historical casualty evidence.

english: Asuras fell, shattered by blows from Vārāhī’s snout, their chests wounded by the tips of her tusks, and cut apart by her discus.
hindi: वाराही की थूथन के प्रहार से चूर, उनके दाँतों की नोक से वक्षस्थल घायल और चक्र से विदीर्ण होकर असुर गिर पड़े।
note: Vārāhī is supplied from the immediately preceding iconographic sequence; the verse’s battle attributes remain source-bound.

english: Nārasiṃhī roamed the battle devouring great asuras torn by her claws, while her roar filled the reaches of every direction.
hindi: नारसिंही अपने नखों से चिरे महासुरों को खाती हुई युद्धभूमि में विचरती रहीं और उनकी गर्जना से दिशाओं के छोर भर गए।
note: The episode’s fierce imagery does not define all Nārasiṃhī worship or iconography.

english: Overwhelmed by Śivadūtī’s fierce laughter, the asuras fell upon the earth; she then devoured them where they lay.
hindi: शिवदूती के प्रचण्ड अट्टहास से विचलित असुर पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़े और तब उन्होंने पड़े हुए असुरों को खा लिया।
note: Abhidūṣita is rendered contextually as overwhelmed or demoralized; the source does not prescribe imitating the action.

english: Seeing the enraged host of Mothers crushing the great asuras by many different means, the soldiers of the gods’ enemies perished.
hindi: क्रुद्ध मातृगण को अनेक उपायों से महासुरों का मर्दन करते देखकर देव-शत्रुओं के सैनिक नष्ट होने लगे।
note: The final verb permits vanished or perished; the battle context supports the latter without asserting literal historical events.

english: Seeing the daityas tormented by the host of Mothers and intent on flight, the great asura Raktabīja advanced in anger to fight.
hindi: मातृगण से पीड़ित दैत्यों को भागने के लिए तत्पर देखकर महासुर रक्तबीज क्रोध में युद्ध करने आगे बढ़ा।
note: This introduces Raktabīja within the episode and does not settle interpretations of his name as allegory.

english: Whenever a drop of blood from his body fell to the ground, a great asura of his own size arose from the earth.
hindi: जब भी उसके शरीर से रक्त की एक बूँद भूमि पर गिरती, उसी के आकार का एक महासुर पृथ्वी से उत्पन्न हो जाता।
note: The replication is a supernatural narrative property, not a biological or medical claim.

english: The great asura, mace in hand, fought with Indra’s śakti; then Aindrī struck Raktabīja with her own thunderbolt.
hindi: हाथ में गदा लिए महासुर ने इन्द्र की शक्ति से युद्ध किया; तब ऐन्द्री ने अपने वज्र से रक्तबीज पर प्रहार किया।
note: The pinned opening compound is joined irregularly; the combat with Aindrī and her thunderbolt strike are clear from syntax and comparison.

english: Struck by the thunderbolt, he swiftly shed abundant blood; from it arose warriors equal to him in form and valour.
hindi: वज्र से घायल होते ही उसके शरीर से बहुत रक्त बहा और उससे उसी के समान रूप तथा पराक्रम वाले योद्धा उत्पन्न हो गए।
note: The duplication remains supernatural episode narration rather than a scientific mechanism.

english: As many drops of blood as fell from his body, that many beings came into existence with his energy, strength, and prowess.
hindi: उसके शरीर से जितनी रक्त-बूँदें गिरीं, उतने ही पुरुष उसके समान तेज, बल और पराक्रम के साथ उत्पन्न हो गए।
note: Puruṣa is rendered as beings or men in this combat population; no universal anthropology is implied.

english: Those blood-born beings also fought there against the Mothers in an exceedingly terrible battle marked by the fall of fierce weapons.
hindi: वे रक्त से उत्पन्न पुरुष भी वहाँ मातृगण के साथ लड़े; उग्र शस्त्रों के प्रहार से वह युद्ध अत्यन्त भयंकर हो उठा।
note: The compact final compound is rendered as the battle’s weapon violence; verse divisions differ in comparison witnesses.

english: When his head was wounded once more by a thunderbolt strike, blood flowed and thousands of beings arose from it.
hindi: जब वज्र के एक और प्रहार से उसका सिर घायल हुआ, तो रक्त बह निकला और उससे हजारों पुरुष उत्पन्न हो गए।
note: The number is epic-scale narration and not treated as independently historical quantity.

english: Vaiṣṇavī struck him in battle with her discus, and Aindrī struck that lord of the asuras with her mace.
hindi: वैष्णवी ने युद्ध में उस पर चक्र से और ऐन्द्री ने उस असुरराज पर गदा से प्रहार किया।
note: The verse’s weapon pairings are retained even though Aindrī’s earlier principal weapon is the thunderbolt.

english: From the blood shed when Vaiṣṇavī’s discus split him, the world was filled with thousands of great asuras equal to him in size.
hindi: वैष्णवी के चक्र से विदीर्ण होने पर बहे रक्त से उसी के आकार वाले हजारों महासुर उत्पन्न हुए और संसार भर गया।
note: The world-filling scale is part of the supernatural narrative and is not literalized as geography or demography.

english: Kaumārī struck the great asura Raktabīja with her spear, Vārāhī with her sword, and Māheśvarī with her trident.
hindi: कौमारी ने शक्ति से, वाराही ने तलवार से और माहेश्वरी ने त्रिशूल से महासुर रक्तबीज पर प्रहार किया।
note: The coordinated śakti actions remain episode-specific and are not extracted as worship instructions.

english: The great asura Raktabīja, possessed by rage, in turn struck each of the Mothers with his mace.
hindi: क्रोध से आविष्ट महासुर रक्तबीज ने भी अपनी गदा से सभी माताओं पर एक-एक करके प्रहार किया।
note: The pinned vocative-looking mātaḥ is understood from context as the Mothers; the source spelling remains unchanged.

english: As he was wounded repeatedly by spears, tridents, and other weapons, the streams of blood that fell from him to the ground produced hundreds of asuras.
hindi: शक्तियों, शूलों और अन्य शस्त्रों से बार-बार घायल होने पर उसके शरीर से जो रक्तधाराएँ भूमि पर गिरीं, उनसे सैकड़ों असुर उत्पन्न हो गए।
note: The pinned middle form is slightly irregular; the blood-causes-replication relation is unambiguous in context.

english: The entire world became filled with those asuras born from the asura’s blood, and the gods then fell into the greatest fear.
hindi: उस असुर के रक्त से उत्पन्न असुरों से समस्त संसार भर गया और तब देवता अत्यन्त भयभीत हो गए।
note: The totalizing scale is epic narration rather than a literal claim about the physical world.

english: Seeing the gods dejected, Caṇḍikā spoke urgently to Kālī: ‘Cāmuṇḍā, open your mouth wide.’
hindi: देवताओं को विषण्ण देखकर चण्डिका ने शीघ्र काली से कहा, ‘हे चामुण्डे, अपना मुख विस्तृत करो।’
note: Kālī is directly addressed as Cāmuṇḍā within the naming continuity of chapter 87; broader identity mappings remain source-scoped.

english: ‘With that swift mouth, catch the drops of blood produced by the blows of my weapons and the great asuras born from those blood-drops.’
hindi: ‘अपने उस वेगवान् मुख से मेरे शस्त्र-प्रहारों से निकली रक्त-बूँदों और उन रक्त-बूँदों से उत्पन्न महासुरों को पकड़ लो।’
note: The source coordination is compressed; the translation preserves both targets—falling blood and the beings it generates—supported by the next verse and comparison witness.

english: ‘Roam the battlefield devouring the great asuras that arise from him. Thus, drained of blood, this daitya will meet his end; as you devour these fierce beings, no others will arise.’
hindi: ‘उससे उत्पन्न महासुरों को खाती हुई युद्धभूमि में विचरो। इस प्रकार रक्त क्षीण हो जाने पर यह दैत्य नष्ट होगा; इन उग्र असुरों को तुम्हारे खा लेने पर और नए असुर उत्पन्न नहीं होंगे।’
